verdict.rationale: Kitty documents its own Terminal graphics protocol, which lets terminal programs render arbitrary pixel (raster) graphics to the screen. It also ships the icat tool, and a community user calls icat a 'must-have', which lightly corroborates hands-on use. missing for 10: detailed evidence of protocol features (image placement, animation, rich-graphics extent) beyond the one-sentence summary, and in-depth independent hands-on verification of the protocol itself.

support.subject: As a developer, I can display inline images and rich graphics via a documented terminal graphics protocol

citations.quote: allows the program running in the terminal, hereafter called the client, to render arbitrary pixel (raster) graphics to the screen of the terminal emulator.
The diff and icat tools are must-haves.
